subject: Performance kickoff: narrowband latency & streaming capacity for Veridian
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@veridianhealth.com>, Amit Rao <amit.rao@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2028 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Performance kickoff: narrowband latency & streaming capacity for Veridian

Hi Claire / Amit —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great questions from your infra team. Per our conversation, I captured the core questions that matter for the p95/p99 E2E acceptance decision (hosted Redwood API vs your current provider):

- Target envelope you asked for: p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 400 ms, 95th-percentile throughput sustain of ~250 qps, with spikes to 400 qps for short bursts.
- Streaming: server-side chunked streaming required for partial-answer UX; client acknowledges chunks every 50–100 tokens.
- Concurrency: expected concurrent user sessions ~120 (peak 180) during business hours.
- Traffic mix: ~65% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (64–512 tokens), 5% long (>512 tokens).

What we committed to next:
1) Upload the traffic envelope you shared (attached) into our hosted test harness and run a 4-hour shadow test across your representative sequence lengths.
2) Run a focused streaming concurrency probe to validate chunking latency and KV-cache hit behavior at 120/180 concurrent sessions.
3) Provide an E2E comparison: current provider metrics (from your post-demo capture) vs Redwood-hosted simulated results (p95/p99 + bandwidth).

I attached a rough SLO table (veridian-slo-table.xlsx) with measurement definitions and proposed canary windows. If the numbers line up, we expect to propose a canary followed by a 7-day shadow run before any cutover.

Action owners / timeline:
- Redwood: Jonas to run the streaming-concurrency probe and share raw histograms by EOD Thu 1/19.
- Veridian: Claire/Amit to confirm whether network egress is restricted (NAT/GW) for the test agents and to provide additional sample payloads by EOD Wed 1/18.
- Both: schedule a 30-min review on Fri 1/20 to review the probe results and define canary windows.

Quick ask: can you confirm whether the 400 qps burst is expected to last longer than 2 minutes? That affects autoscaling choices.

Thanks —
Diego
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: veridian-slo-table.xlsx (xlsx), traffic-envelope-20280117.json (json)
From: Claire Park <cpark@veridianhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Rao <amit.rao@veridianhealth.com>, Veridian Ops <ops@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jan 2028 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance kickoff: narrowband latency & streaming capacity for Veridian

Diego —

Appreciate the summary, this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- Bursts: the 400 qps is typically short — 45–90s in our historic windowed traffic. Rarely exceeds 2 minutes.
- Network: test agents will originate from our us-west NAT pool (10.1.0.0/22 -> egress via gw-prod-usw1). We can open temporary ACLs for your IP block if needed.
- Current provider baseline: we measured p95=210ms, p99=620ms E2E (includes client->provider network). We will share the raw histograms (attaching the JSON traffic envelope).

Also: our engineering team emphasized TLS handshake overhead on cold sessions — they want to see warm and cold-run splits. Can your probe script split samples into warm (KV cache primed) and cold (cache empty) so we can compare tail behavior?

I'll confirm an internal slot for Fri 1/20 09:00 PT; Amit will drop in the ops folks for ACLs/egress details.

Thanks,
Claire
Director, Platform Engineering — Veridian Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@veridianhealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jan 2028 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance kickoff: narrowband latency & streaming capacity for Veridian

Claire —

Thanks for the histograms — I looked through the sample envelope. A few technical notes on how we'll structure the probe so metrics are comparable to your capture:

- Measurement boundaries: we'll capture E2E from our test agent (in your VPC egress) to the final token emitted by the hosted model and include the streaming chunk latencies. That should line up with your current provider capture.
- Warm vs cold: probe will run two pass types — (A) cold sessions (fresh process, empty KV cache) and (B) warm sessions (KV cache pre-populated with preceding 5 requests matching session prefix). We'll report p50/p95/p99 for both.
- Autoscale smoothing: for the 45–90s bursts, we'll test two autoscale profiles: 30s ramp and 90s ramp to show the impact on p99 during bursts.
- Tokenization mix: we'll replicate your mix (65/30/5) and also run a 100% short prompt control to isolate streaming overhead.

Deliverables by Thu EOD (1/19):
- Raw histograms (t-digest) for cold/warm passes.
- Streaming chunk latency CDFs (per-token and per-chunk).
- Recommendation for canary sizing and an initial SLA gap table (hosted vs incumbent).

Jonas
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 20 Jan 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance kickoff: narrowband latency & streaming capacity for Veridian

Claire — thanks for the quick turn. Short update and confirmed next steps before our Fri 09:00 PT sync:

- Jonas ran the probe overnight against the envelope you provided (traffic-envelope-20280117.json). Summary:
  • Redwood-hosted (default autoscale): p95=138ms, p99=375ms (E2E, warm).
  • Redwood-hosted (cold-heavy profile): p95=210ms, p99=510ms.
  • Incumbent (Veridian-provided capture): p95=210ms, p99=620ms (your numbers match).

- Streaming chunking: per-chunk latency median=28ms, p95=95ms. Chunk size matches your client (approx 80 tokens per chunk).
- Burst handling: with a 30s autoscale ramp, p99 spikes to ~780ms at 400 qps bursts; with a 90s ramp p99 stays ~420–480ms. This illustrates the tradeoff you flagged around ramp windows.

Attached: raw histograms + the gap table in the SLO sheet. High-level interpretation: Redwood-hosted meets your targeted p95 goal on warm sessions and is within ~20% of p99 target on warm runs; cold-heavy traffic is closer to incumbent for p95 but has a tighter p99.

Proposed canary plan (if you want to proceed):
- Canary window: 48 hours with 15% of real traffic shadowed through Redwood-hosted routing.
- Autoscale profile: start with 90s ramp, evaluate if we can tighten to 45s after observing burst behavior.
- Success criteria: warm p95 <=150ms AND warm p99 <=400ms for at least 95% of the 48-hour window.

Action items for Fri sync at 09:00 PT:
- Veridian: confirm ACLs and allowlist for Redwood test agents.
- Veridian: provide a sample of TLS cold-session handshake logs if possible (to help root cause cold tail).
- Redwood: present raw histograms and propose canary start time.

If that all sounds good I can drop a calendar invite for 09:00 PT and attach the SLO sheet + histograms.

Diego
